text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch central bank DNB raises special rate on advances to boost guilder against D-mark. (p1)
- Amsterdam stock exchange and EOE options exchange failed in supervision of Nusse Brink brokerage, says finance minister Gerrit Zalm in a letter to parliament. (p1)
- Anglo-Dutch computer systems company CMG expects further profit growth in 1997 after strong 1996. (p1)
- Food and drinks group BolsWessanen says selling 35 pct stake in Italian drinks concern Campari is realistic option. (p1)
- Cabinet gives green light for four of six proposed technological top institutes on condition that industry raises contribution. (p1)
- Interior furnishings company Blydenstein-Willink books Dfl 2.9 million losses in 1996; company positive about future prospects.
- Rabobank's leasing and factoring subsidiary De Lage Landen books strong foreign growth. (p4)
- Dutch industry reports four percent turnover growth in January compared with the year-earlier period. (p5)
VOLKSKRANT
- Parliament wants cabinet to limit media magnates' power over radio-stations. (p1)
- Banks unable to handle increasing interest in stocks. (p2)
- FNV union criticises brewer Heineken for endangering life of staff by ignoring embargo against Burundi. (p2)
- Publisher VNU to restructure Dutch magazines group. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Builder Volker Stevin takes over rival Kondor Wessels, creating combine with four billion guilders turnover. (p1)
- Dutch tourist authority starts offensive to lure back German tourists. (p3)
- Beer consumption in Netherlands in 1996 drops to 83.7 litres per person. (p7)
- Amsterdam shopkeepers threaten to disturb Euro summit in June as protest against growing criminality. (p8)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- CMG had to let go orders because of lack of personnel. (p10)
- Tension mounts at Fokker over a possible re-launch of the bankrupt aircraft maker. (p11)
TROUW
- McCain to build the world's largest French fries plant in Lelystad. (p7)
- Christian union CFO exceeds rival Christian union CNV's wages demands for Dutch PTT KPN staff. (p7)
